methodological_rigor.justification: Comprehensive integrative analysis of 124 thymomas + 13 thymic carcinomas: 20 newly sequenced cases plus 117 from public datasets. Combined genomic and transcriptomic data with single-cell RNA-seq from developmental murine thymus tissues. Stratification methodology well-defined (GTF2I mutation status, copy-number alterations, mutational burden, cellular origin assignment). However: sample size justification absent, batch correction methodology across public datasets not detailed, no independent validation cohort.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Three-subgroup classification (GTF2I-type, CN-type, thymic carcinomas) may guide therapeutic stratification (GTF2I-targeted therapy, immune-based approaches per phenotype). However, clinical outcome correlation (survival, response) not assessed. Therapeutic impact speculative pending outcome validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods describe sequencing platforms, reference databases (MANE, GENCODE, COSMIC, GEO), and integration approach. Missing: explicit batch correction methodology, quality control metrics for multi-source data integration, complete statistical thresholds for clustering/classification, outcome and phenotype correlation analyses.

novelty_literature.justification: Integrated genomic/transcriptomic classification revealing three distinct thymic epithelial tumor subgroups with different cellular origins (progenitors, differentiated TEC, tuft cells) and evolutionary trajectories. Single-cell murine developmental reference enhances origin assignment. Novel disease-specific classification framework.

writing_presentation.justification: Abstract comprehensive summarizing three-group stratification. Methods likely well-organized for complex integrative analysis. Some density in genomic/transcriptomic methodology sections appropriate for specialized audience.

key_strengths: Comprehensive integrative analysis combining newly sequenced cohort (n=137) with large public dataset (n=117) for robust subgroup classification
Single-cell murine thymic developmental transcriptomics integrated to identify putative cellular origins of each TET subgroup
Three distinct subgroups identified with clear molecular signatures (GTF2I mutations, copy-number patterns, mutational burden) and differential transcriptional/immune phenotypes
Evolutionary pathway analysis: early copy-number alterations in CN-type suggesting distinct tumorigenic trajectories across subgroups
key_concerns: Batch correction approach not explicitly detailed for integration of newly sequenced and public samples; potential for technical confounding
No independent external validation: classification performance tested only on included samples
Clinical outcome correlation absent: survival, recurrence, therapeutic response not assessed; therapeutic impact speculative
Statistical testing minimal: no formal significance testing of subgroup differences or association with outcomes
Murine single-cell thymic origin mapping may not reliably predict human TET cellular origins given developmental differences
chief_reviewer.rationale: Novel disease-specific classification with rigorous integrative approach. Clinical outcome validation needed for tier 2, supporting tier 3 placement.
